history: Found as an ORACLE/COMPILER ACCEPT SPLIT. codegen refused; interp.Interpreter.run did [0] * arr.length with no limit at all, so interpret_source -- a public entry point exported in replayc.__all__ -- accepted the same program and allocated 800 MB for it, and one more zero was a MemoryError, which is neither a Trap nor a refusal. The oracle is documented as carrying 'the SAME totality as the machine' and was missing a bound the machine has. Note the residual: the parse-time guard compares the array length against MAX_MEM without counting the cells the program's own scalars need, so lengths of exactly 1048575 and 1048576 still parse and then fail in codegen. See 009.
note: MAX_MEM is 1,048,576 cells -- replay.py: '1M cells. A receipt is a document, not a workload.' A program asking for a hundred times that is refused before either lowering runs it, so the oracle and the compiler agree about which programs exist.
source: input a; arr m[99999999]; output a;
